docs.purpose: Shows an admin the history of the last twenty permit-data import runs, and lets them manually trigger a new import of permit data from a file already sitting on the server.
docs.data_story: It reads 5 tables — `sync_runs`, `trade_mapping_rules`, `trades`, `permit_type_classifications` and `permits` and writes `sync_runs`, `permits`, `permit_trades` and `permit_history`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 12 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables. It mutates admin state and writes **no `admin_audit_log` row** — one of the nine measured gaps Phase 0 closes.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `COMMAND`. It declares the JOB it triggers (`job_ref`), its concurrency posture and the audit row it must write. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

notes: No SPEC LINK and no verifyAdminAuth import — relies entirely on blanket route-guard.ts. POST accepts a raw file_path string from the body with no validation or allow-listing before it reaches runSync -> parsePermitsStream (src/lib/sync/process.ts, src/lib/sync/ingest.ts) — a local-file-path surface with no visible sanitization in this file. runSync executes the whole multi-record ingest synchronously in-process inside this one HTTP request, in contrast to pipelines/[slug], whose comments explain long-running work was deliberately moved off Vercel onto GitHub Actions. No writeAdminAudit despite being a bulk data-mutating operation. No in-repo caller found. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS, worst first. (1) ARBITRARY LOCAL FILE READ BEHIND NO ROUTE-LEVEL AUTH: POST (:37) takes `body.file_path` (:40), validates only that it is a non-empty string (:42), and passes it to runSync (:50) -> parsePermitsStream (src/lib/sync/process.ts:339) -> `createReadStream(filePath)` (src/lib/sync/ingest.ts:28). There is no verifyAdminAuth, no path confinement, no CSRF Origin check. Content is stream-JSON-parsed, so a non-matching file mostly errors rather than exfiltrating — but the open() itself is caller-controlled and the route is guarded only by src/middleware.ts:115's presence-only check. (2) MISSING GUARD generally: no verifyAdminAuth on either method, against src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:9-11's MUST. (3) SELECT * — TWO sites, both inside the POST path: src/lib/sync/process.ts:28 (trade_mapping_rules) and src/lib/sync/process.ts:97 (permits, executed once per record streamed, in batches of 5000 — src/lib/sync/ingest.ts:22). Columns recorded as 'all' for both. (4) POST returns `RETURNING *` sync_runs rows (src/lib/sync/process.ts:325, :361, :389) spread straight into the response at :52. (5) ENVELOPE DEVIATION: five bare responses (see envelope.deviations). (6) A failed sync returns HTTP 200 (src/lib/sync/process.ts:378-402 returns the failed row; route :52 wraps it) — a caller that checks only the status code sees success. (7) No audit row for a mutation that can rewrite the entire permits table. (8) CENSUS AGREES: census_reads [sync_runs, trade_mapping_rules, trades, permit_type_classifications, permits] and census_writes [sync_runs, permits, permit_trades, permit_history] are all confirmed at the lines above — nothing in the census is unfindable, nothing extra found.
